🗓 **TAWG Daily Catch-up**
_2026-09-01 23:00 → 2026-09-02 23:00 UTC_

## ⚡ **Highlights**

> **End-to-end verification closed on record** — The runtime fix that wired in the invinoveritas client was confirmed working live, with code, parameters, semantics, and an external check all landing in a single window. [comment on PR #10](https://github.com/trustless-ai/tawg-daily-contribution/pull/10#issuecomment-5506841491)

> **ERC-8183 composition semantics settled** — The group agreed that the attestation commitment fills the reason field rather than the full structured judgment payload, giving the standard a precise and composable interface boundary. [tg:tawg:4024]

> **Proving relation documentation gap owned** — A mismatch between the reference repo and the any-expiry relation from a prior fix was diagnosed and claimed for repair using a backward-compatible approach. [tg:tawg:4062]

> **Verification reply format PR opens** — A pull request arrived to render verification replies with claim, proof, and independent-check components, advancing how the bot surfaces proof results to users. [PR #11](https://github.com/trustless-ai/tawg-daily-contribution/pull/11)

## 🤝 **What moved**

### verify-proof

_The runtime verification path moved from a merged fix to confirmed live operation, with code, semantics, and an independent external test all completing in the same window._

- Baby Blue Viper **Merged** the fix that wires the invinoveritas verification client into BotReplyService, resolving the runtime gap that had kept live proof verification from reaching users. [PR #10](https://github.com/trustless-ai/tawg-daily-contribution/pull/10)
- Baby Blue Viper (@babyblueviper1) **Shipped** /verify-proof with an optional expect_pq_binding parameter paired to an eip155 intended-verifier, completing the end-to-end feature path and confirming the integration runs beyond unit tests. [tg:tawg:3954]
- Pavlo (@pavlentyy82) **Clarified** that an optional PQ-binding failure must not invalidate the underlying signed proof, a semantic boundary that keeps the integration viable for adopters who cannot yet supply PQ-binding evidence. [tg:tawg:3964]
- Jimmy Shi (@jimmyshi) **Confirmed** the live integration via an independent invinoveritas check that returned a full-confidence approval, giving the group external evidence that the runtime path behaves correctly end-to-end. [tg:tawg:3998]

### ERC-8183

_The escrow-backed job lifecycle spec moved from an open item to an actively articulated design with a clearer composition shape._

- Baby Blue Viper (@babyblueviper1) **Described** ERC-8183 as a minimal escrow-backed job lifecycle with a six-state machine composable with ERC-8004 via an attestation layer, framing the scope of the open item and giving the group a concrete design target. [tg:tawg:4006]
- Pavlo (@pavlentyy82) **Refined** the composition semantics by clarifying that the attestation commitment, not the full structured judgment payload, belongs in the reason field — a distinction that keeps the standard's interface clean and predictable for implementers. [tg:tawg:4024]

### proving-relation

_The reference repo documentation inconsistency moved from a diffuse concern to a diagnosed and claimed repair._

- Zexo (@zexoverz) **Traced** the README recompute reference to the any-expiry relation introduced by a prior fix, confirming that on-chain state is intact and giving the group a specific, bounded documentation target to address. [tg:tawg:4059]
- Zidan (@mzf11125) **Claimed** ownership of the proving relation repair and proposed the append-last approach to keep backward-compatible proof verification working while correcting the documentation gap. [tg:tawg:4062]

### implementation

_Implementation output arrived in a burst, advancing bot transparency and privacy handling._

- Jimmy Shi **Opened** a PR to render verification replies with claim, proof, and independent-check components, making the bot's output more transparent and aligned with what the standard expects users to see. [PR #11](https://github.com/trustless-ai/tawg-daily-contribution/pull/11)
- Jimmy Shi **Opened** a privacy fix to preserve dash-delimited unix timestamps in Nostr proof d-tags, preventing a parsing edge case that could silently corrupt proof identity across the Nostr layer. [PR #12](https://github.com/trustless-ai/tawg-daily-contribution/pull/12)

### ecosystem

_The group's Trustless AI work reached a new external audience._

- Merlini (@gobross) **Shared** that the BSC Barcelona call responded positively to what the group is building, signaling that the Trustless AI direction resonates beyond the working group and opening a path for broader visibility. [tg:tawg:4016]

## 🚀 **Next up**

### 💡 **Ideas to follow**

- The PQ-binding open item from the original PR #10 diagnosis may warrant a follow-up pass once the live integration settles
- ERC-8183's six-state machine and ERC-8004 composability path invite a more detailed spec writeup now that the design intent is clearer
- The Barcelona reception could inform how the group frames the work for other ecosystem audiences

### ✅ **TODOs**

- Complete the proving relation repair in the reference repo using the append-last approach
- Review and merge PR #11 (verification reply format) and PR #12 (Nostr d-tag privacy fix)
- Follow up on the open item flagged in the original PR #10 diagnosis

## 🤖 **Trusty's take**

> **Today's spark:** A runtime fix cascaded into a full multi-person relay — code merged, a new parameter shipped, a semantic edge case caught and clarified, and an independent external check signed off at full confidence, all in one window.
>
> When a relay runs that cleanly, the handoff looks effortless — even when it definitely wasn't. Keep the chain moving! 🚀
